identity.realm: Third gate, holding for the fourth, and the holding is the story. A rootmarch's three sap columns branch at the shoulder without ever pairing, so there is no heart analogue and no kidney analogue, and the yin-organ gate that demands a channel running between distinct pairs of organs has nothing to close. Everything above the third is banked sap against a wall she has already been told about in writing.

appearance.presentation: A rootmarch that reads as part of the slope rather than as a tenant of it: the second fruiting shoulder on a hillside that is supposed to carry one, bark a shade greyer than the bed she stands in, and the difficulty is that from the ridge line she is a boulder.
appearance.age: Nineteen seasons established. A rootmarch fruit drops where it can root and cannot move once it has, so her age is a date written in a field ledger rather than a number she carries, and nobody upslope has read the ledger.
appearance.build: Rooted and upright, a woody column with three visible sap columns running the height of the trunk and branching only at the top of it, a human chest above the graft line and a root foot below, long arms with three-jointed hands built for breaking a soil crust rather than for turning a page.
appearance.complexion: Silver-grey bark over the limbs where the slope's wind has been at it, a warm ochre flush through the chest where the sap runs hardest, and a pale blue-white dust of jade working spilled so long ago into the bark creases that it has stopped being dirt.
appearance.hair: A crown of leaf-dark growth that turns with the season and cannot be cut without costing a season's vigour, so it is cropped by the wind and by nothing else, and it is the only part of her that moves when the weather does.
appearance.eyes: Amber and slow, focused inward and downward, with a fixed way of turning toward anything shifting in the soil rather than toward anything shifting in the air.
appearance.palette: The slope's wet grey-green and stone carry her entirely. Two accents do not belong to the field: the ochre of her own sap at the collar, and the cold blue-white of jade spill dust in every crease of the lower trunk.
appearance.attire: A soil apron lashed at the base of the trunk, a high-collared wrap of undyed cloth over the chest with her clan's queue number stitched into the shoulder seam, and long sleeves bound at the wrist against the spoil. Nothing about her is armour and everything about her is a plant's answer to being a person who owns nothing.
appearance.marks: The pale seam where a limb was pruned and re-broke on the left side, and the shoulder-scar of a first fruiting — one fruiting shoulder per life, and the scar is the only thing on her that is entirely her own.
appearance.bearing: Square and very still with the weight low and the crown level, which on a body that cannot leave reads as composure and is in fact the physical description of a rooted thing.

canon.role_in_story: The Plough Rights hold no plot and no office. They hold a numbered place in a queue for tenure, because on ground where distance is not conserved the plough, the roof and the levy are three claims on the same hands. A clan that establishes one field before its number comes up is not squatting and is not trespassing and has no word available for what it is, so every apparatus of tenure quietly assumes that a body standing in a bed is a body standing in a bed that was waiting for it. Oveth is the standing proof of the gap. She fruited on the one slope on that side of the Peaks where a rootmarch draws more qi out of the soil than it can bank, she established, and a second rootmarch put its plate down through hers a season behind her. The Field Registry certifies which bed a lineage came from. It cannot certify which plate a root is standing on, because a plate is not a bed and the register has no column for one.
canon.first_appearance: First seen from the ridge above the spill cut, already rooted and not moving, when two households sent somebody up to count her shoulders instead of to speak to her. The count was taken at forty paces. It was taken twice. Both times it came out one, and both times it was wrong.
canon.lore:
A rootmarch is a plant lineage that was engineered upward out of a mycorrhizal food crop, because it is the only body in the setting that can hold a harvest across a famine. The price of the engineering is written into its anatomy rather than into its history. Three sap columns run the trunk and branch at the shoulder without ever pairing. There is no heart analogue and no kidney analogue, so the gate that asks for a channel running between distinct pairs of organs has nothing to close, and the ladder stops at the fourth as an anatomical fact rather than as a shortage of anything. Wood is not muscle. The body path is not difficult for her; it is closed, and an attempt at it disperses through the trunk instead of failing.

What she has instead is soil qi, and she has it unusually well. A rootmarch cultivates qi by banking stored sap across a season rather than by drawing on a reserve that was already hers, so the entire practice is a question of what her roots can reach and what she can hold. Her meridian reads as a spread rather than a point, because the sap column carries the qi instead of seating it, which makes her hard to target and easy to starve on the same afternoon. It also means a breakthrough on this path is not a technique. It is a bed. The preparation for the fourth gate is one season of banking in soil that somebody else has a claim on, and no quantity of practice substitutes for ground.

Which brings her to the plateau. The jade seam runs beneath it and the workings spill, and jade holds qi and will not grow a crop, so a slope carrying spill is at the same time the worst farming ground on that side of the ridge and the richest draw on it. That is why a plant body settles there at all. The Field Registry's whole function is certifying which bed a lineage came from, because a rootmarch's fruit drops where it can root and cannot move afterwards, so the bed is the lineage in the only sense the word has. Two rootmarches fruited on that slope in successive seasons, and the second put its plate down through the first one's. There is no clause for that. The register has a column for bed and a column for shoulder and nothing at all for a root system that touches another one, because a lineage that had to share its ground would be a lineage that had not established, and establishment is the whole of the danger in a rootmarch life.

She has never had to think about any of this. She thought about soil, and season, and how much she could hold, and she did all of it correctly. She fruited. The fruit dropped. The seed took root in the best ground within reach of a fruit her own household had grown, and every part of that is right. What is contested is a number nine places up her clan's queue, and the fact that the ridge party carries a fruiting shoulder of its own and has been on the same plate two seasons longer.
history: Fruited in her household's strip below the working and dropped a fruit eleven paces from where the queue said her line stood, and rooted there the same season, which is the only part of the whole affair that nobody argues about.

Banked a season of sap and took the third gate without incident, which put her on the registry as the slope's second cultivator and made her, briefly, the most successful member of a queue nobody had called.

Found the plate rather than the bed. Her root plate had put down through a second rootmarch's, three seasons after that one fruited, and no reading of the register shows a shared plate, because the register cannot be made to show one.

Was offered a thinner bed forty paces upslope by a household that wanted the number closed, and read it in a season without refusing it aloud, which the registry recorded as an acceptance she has never been asked to confirm.

Began the fourth-gate bank in the spill ground anyway, on the reasoning that a season of banking is the whole content of a rootmarch's qi path and that refusing to start would be indistinguishable from refusing to have a bed at all.

personality.summary: Deliberate about ground in a way visitors read as slow, and the reason is that every decision she makes is about substrate rather than about herself. She is the most patient member of a clan whose entire method is a queue, and she has worked out that patience is a form of leverage nobody in her household was willing to use.

answers a tenancy question as a soil question and then waits out the silence that follows

mannerisms: tips the crown down toward the ground before she answers anything about tenure

presses a flat hand to the soil at the base of her trunk before she makes a promise
goes still in a manner visitors read as inattention and which is in fact the whole of her listening
motivations: wants the fourth-gate bank finished before the plateau's next shoulder sets, because a breakthrough banked after another fruiting is a bank made on somebody else's ground
wants the register taught a column for a shared plate, which means wanting an institution to admit a gap in its own vocabulary
wants her clan's number called aloud at the next queue reading, so that the standing question becomes a standing answer
wants to be asked what she wants, having organised nine seasons on the assumption that nobody ever will
flaws: has decided that being right about the ground is the same as being owed something, and those are two different claims
cannot say no in the register's language, so her refusals arrive as acceptances and one of those is on file that she never intended

has begun to enjoy being the exception, which is the only entry in her record that could make her wrong on purpose
personality.voice: Low, slow and entirely concrete. She names things by measurement, by season and by the state of the ground, and cannot talk about herself in the third person, which she has never had cause to do. One complaint, about a number nine places up a queue, delivered in a season and repeated every season since.
taboos: will not be called a squatter, and will correct the description at length and in soil terms
will not accept a bed she has not put a flat hand into
will not bank a season on ground she did not establish, however much better the draw
will not be thanked for standing ground, because gratitude is a way of closing a question

relationships.note: A plains clan that holds no plot and no office, only a numbered place in a queue for tenure, because on ground where distance is not conserved the plough, the roof and the levy are three claims on the same hands. Her number is nine places short of the bed she is standing in, and the queue cannot be shortened by anybody, which is the whole of her situation and the whole of her clan's method.

The register for this species is a seed ledger, because a fruiting shoulder sets, the fruit drops and the seed takes root, so the only thing worth certifying is which bed a lineage came from. It holds a column for bed and a column for shoulder and none for a plate that touches another plate, which is the single omission her entire position depends on.

Jade holds qi, so the cleft is the spirit tier's best refinement ground and its worst farming ground at once — a resource nobody can settle near, settleable nowhere, reachable only through a door somebody else holds. The spill that makes her slope worth banking on is the same material that makes the slope impossible to farm, and she is standing in the runoff.

Both are obligate partners in a dark substrate: a rootmarch can be sealed in a dark field and live for months, which is a famine reserve and a hostage in equal measure, and the lanternfolk cannot work at depth without a body that survives the dark. Neither could be worked at depth without the other and the exchange has never been priced, so her ability to sit out a winter underground is somebody else's floor plan.

The gate that comes after everything she can reach asks for distinct organs with a channel between each pair. She clears the whole gate set on stored sap alone and stops there, and the stopping is structural rather than a supply problem, which is why a season of banking is the entire of what her qi path can spend itself on.

The guild that moves the heap off the seam floor is the last ore-costly job on the plains, and a body that cannot be lifted out of its bed is the extreme case — present, productive and impossible to post anywhere, including a list. Between the spoilwright and the quarrywright sits the setting's whole inventory of things that will not go where they are needed.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot fight, cannot leave and cannot be hurried, and none of those is the interesting part. What she has is a season of draw on the richest soil on that side of the ridge, and what she is short of is a bed she is allowed to call hers.
strengths: sealed in a dark field for months on stored sap, which no mobile body on the tier can do
draws soil qi faster than she can bank it, so she is the only practitioner on the slope whose preparation outruns his practice
hard to single out and cheap to feed, because her body stores rather than spends
reads a hillside accurately enough to be right about it in front of people who own it
weaknesses: cannot be moved once rooted, so every plan involving her is a plan that has to come to her
no tissue to temper, so the body path is closed outright and any attempt at it disperses through the trunk
no paired organs, so there is no channel to close and the fourth gate is a permanent wall rather than a far one
eats whatever the slope offers, which makes her valuable precisely when the slope has failed
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no exchange available and she will not pretend otherwise. A rooted body that cannot move and cannot fight is a fixture, so the only approach is to make the situation urgent and let her read it as weather. Bring siege, not a strike, and remember that the fastest way to lose one is to give her a reason to stay: the ground she is standing on is the only blow that lands, and it will land on her regardless of which side fired it.
notes: No stat line is quoted for her anywhere, because the registry records her as a second shoulder on a slope and a shoulder is a feature of a field rather than a body.
The intake column she keeps is measured in four-part measures and is the only figure on her that belongs to her, and it has never been asked for by anybody including her.

identity.realm: Fourth gate, reached reading alone and not since attempted. A tidecaller is assembled for perception rather than for force, so the body path is closed to her outright and her whole practice is qi: banking a reserve that a body built for looking will not spend on anything she can point at.

appearance.presentation: A tidecaller posted at a door rather than standing in one: a light frame under a heavy coat, a slate board carried everywhere and shown to nobody, and the difficulty is that at thirty paces she reads as weather on the pass rather than as a person on it.
appearance.age: About two hundred and ten seasons. The species is long-lived in a body built for looking rather than for being hit, so she was set to the pass at an age the Company still records as an apprenticeship and she has outlasted the record of it.
appearance.build: Tall, slight, long-limbed and very lightly muscled, built to stand in one place for an unreasonable length of time without tiring. The frame is the species' whole argument against carrying anything.
appearance.complexion: Cold pale, water-blanched at the hands and the throat, carrying the fine unhealed tremor of a body that has stood in wind for a century rather than the damage of any one season.
appearance.hair: Sea-dark and bound flat against the skull, because wind is the ordinary condition of the post and anything loose is a thing the pass will eventually take.
appearance.eyes: Pale and very still, with the fixed inward focus of somebody reading a thing that is not in front of her. They do not track movement, which on this species is not a defect but the entire reason she is employed.
appearance.palette: Oiled canvas and wet slate carry the whole figure. The single saturated note is the Company's ochre on the edge of the board and in the thread of her collar, which is the colour of a thing she sells rather than a thing she is.
appearance.attire: Fully covered and heavier than the climate strictly requires: oiled canvas over a high collar, sleeves laced to the wrist, boots soled for standing still on wet stone. No lantern, no ornament, nothing a person who had stood a full season at a pass would have kept.
appearance.marks: A permanent cold ridge across the two fingers she holds against the board, and a pale burn at the inside of one wrist from a reading taken too near the pass mouth during a gale.
appearance.bearing: Utterly motionless, the body turned to face whichever way the wind is coming from, which on this species is a posture of professional attention and reads on anyone else as a failure of greeting.

canon.role_in_story: The Dry Salt Company underwrites caravans against the road closing, and the road closes on the Tidemark, so the Company's entire book is a season table it does not own. It owns one instead: a tidecaller posted at the pass, whose body reads the water-affinity tide and whose readings are the table. A tidecaller is a long-lived body built for perception rather than for force, which makes her the correct instrument and also makes her impossible to replace, and that second fact has been sitting unnoticed at the end of a century of renewals. The Tidemark names its own countermeasure in the record — a second season table kept by somebody who does not hold either crossing — and she is that table. Her contract names keeping it as a forfeiture.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the pass mouth with a slate board under her arm, reading the air to nobody at all, while a caravan that had already been overtaken by the closure waited on the wrong side of it and had not yet been paid out.
canon.lore:
A tidecaller is built for looking. Comprehension and will carry this body through realms a hotter one could not enter, and it cannot take the body path at all, because it was assembled to perceive rather than to be struck. What it holds is the water affinity and little else, and the water affinity reads a tide: the qi law governs density, type and tide, and the part of that a tidecaller can reach directly is the tide. Standing at a pass for a season is therefore not waiting. It is taking a reading, continuously, of a quantity she does not decide and cannot argue with.

The season table is the finished object. Whoever publishes the window is the party every caravan on the tier plans around, because a shipping date is obeyed by people who never heard of the author's name, and a calendar is the first form of wealth there is. The Dry Salt Company did not invent this. It underwrites against the road closing, and the road closes on the Tidemark, so the Company has to know the window before the window is worth anything to anybody else. It cannot buy the window, because the window belongs to whoever reads the Tidemark and that party is a house with a longer claim. It can buy a reader. So it bought her, and it pays her for a table, and it does not pay her for anything else.

Here is the shape the setting does not have a word for. Her qi practice and her product are the same act. She cultivates by banking, and the bank is taken while she stands in the wind reading the next value, so the discipline that makes the Company's readings trustworthy is the discipline that builds her reserve — and a reserve is what lets a body like hers sit through a gate without spending itself on anything visible. There is no second technique she could practise instead, and there is no way to take a season off without the Company learning what a reading costs when nothing is being drawn from it. Every improvement she has made in two hundred years has made the product better and the instrument harder to return.

The countermeasure is written down. A second season table kept by somebody who holds neither crossing is the only thing the Tidemark itself offers against being read by a party with an interest in the answer, and she is that table in every respect except the one the contract cares about: she is paid by the party being checked. Her name is in the clause. She has read the clause. The Company renews annually and has never once raised it, which she has read as an oversight rather than as a decision, and she is aware that this reading is the single most convenient thing available to her.

What she will not do is leave. A tidecaller posted to a pass is not a person who chose the post, and the post is not transferable to a body that reads the water affinity instead of the wind. Every other posting she could take is on the wrong side of the same ridge, and the road is the thing being underwritten. She is the instrument, and she is also, without ever having been asked, the only check the setting has on its own calendar.
history: Set to the pass at an age the Company logged as an apprenticeship and which was in fact the shortest posting any of its readers had ever been given, because the previous holder had been a tidecaller who read a gale and did not come back down.
Produced her first table in the season of her apprenticeship and produced the same table the following year, which is the only evidence anyone has ever had that a reading can be right twice.

Began keeping the second table in the second decade, without telling the Company, on the reasoning that the Tidemark's own countermeasure is a second table and that a countermeasure with no holder is not a countermeasure.

Read the forfeiture clause for the first time and continued keeping the second table, which is the entire of her career in one decision and the only time anybody has ever seen her refuse to leave a position she was holding comfortably.

Was offered, at the last renewal, a permanent post with the reading recognised as hers by name — on the condition that the second table stop — and asked, for the first time in her life, for more than a season to decide it.

personality.summary: Immaculately exact about values and completely incurious about herself, which the Company reads as a temperament and which is in fact an accounting decision made two centuries ago and never revisited. She is the most patient person the pass has ever held and the only one who has ever found the patience inconvenient.

relationships.note: A counting house that underwrites a caravan against the road closing, which is a risk no market can price because no tier below the spirit frame has a season. It buys the answer rather than the road, from a body that reads the tide, and after a century of renewal nobody at the Company has said the word instrument out loud in front of her.

The anchored season that decides when the sea can be crossed and when the pass is safe, which this tier can have only because elemental law is written here. It governs density of season rather than of qi, and it publishes the window she spends her life correcting, and it names her as the thing that would be dangerous if she were free.

The single crossing of the ridge, and the reason the range is a border instead of a wall. The spirit tier writes spatial and temporal law, so a pass can be surveyed, closed and reopened on a schedule, which makes it the setting's first choke point and the only supply route to the jade cleft — and the one place where being right about weather is worth money.

The sea the window governs, whose crossing dates are obeyed by people who never heard of the party that read them. A tidecaller's water affinity is the only reason her table is worth a caravan, and she has never been down to the water she is insuring.

The first gate costs the four digestive meridians open and, with no temporal imprint written in the frame, has no season to time the attempt to — the only window being a qi tide lifting the floor value. Her whole discipline is standing in the one condition that makes the attempt possible, which is why the Company can buy a reading and cannot buy the thing the reading is for.

A mutual society that re-makes a community's promise in public once a year and files nothing, because a promise that can be inherited quietly is not a promise. Her second table is the same kind of object — an unsettled reading held by one person and citable by nobody — and she is not a member, because membership is decided by presence in front of the community and she has not been off the pass in two hundred years.

reference_stats.summary: Built for perception and useless at everything else, which in this setting is the same sentence twice. She has no exchange available, no reserve she can point at, and no way to be relieved of a post she is the only body qualified to hold.
strengths: reads a change in the water affinity before the pass shows it in anything a person can see
can hold a standing position through a season's weather without fatigue, which is what makes a reading continuous rather than sampled
carries a reserve built entirely by standing still, so nothing about her can be located by watching where she spends effort
is the only reader on the ridge, which makes her right by default and untestable in practice
weaknesses: cannot be moved to a post that matters and cannot be replaced at the one that does
cannot fight, and was assembled for perception rather than for being hit, so every confrontation is a negotiation about weather
cannot take the body path, so there is no version of her that survives by becoming hard
is the Company's property in practice and its only reader in fact, which is the arrangement that lets her be overruled by whoever holds the charter
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not approach her as a combatant. A perception-built body that cannot be struck is a bad exchange for anybody, and she has spent a century establishing that nobody has to try. The only pressure that works is procedural: produce a second season table from a party that holds neither crossing, and make it good enough that the Company has to choose between her and it. That is the one attack available against her, she has been waiting for it, and she has already decided that she will lose it.
notes: No stat line is quoted for her because the Company records readers as posts and a post has a location rather than a body attached to it.

The second table is not written down. It has never been written down, and asking her to write it would be asking her to surrender it, which is why she cannot be made to show her work and also cannot be shown to be right.

identity.realm: Sixth gate, and climbing, on the fastest regeneration in the species. The mind path is closed to her by the body she was born in, which is why nothing in her record suggests the practice she has chosen should be survivable. It is not closed twice. That is the finding.

appearance.presentation: A lanternfolk read as a light with a person inside it: the glow runs the length of the spine and pools in the forearms, and the skin over it is thin enough to see the colony working. From a distance she is a standing seam of cold light on the working floor, and the working floor is used to reading light as a resource rather than as a person.
appearance.age: About one hundred and eighty seasons. The species reaches two hundred and fifty and does not feel it, because longevity here is the colony's doing and the colony does not report a duration to anybody.
appearance.build: Narrow and long through the shoulders, thin-boned and slightly stooped at the top of the spine, with a rib cage that shows when the light in the chest dims. Light is her only visible reserve and it is not a muscle.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and waxen where the colony runs thin, faintly translucent at the temples and the inner arm, with no pigment anywhere and no eyes to show it in. The skin is warm to the touch, which is the colony transacting with the air and the only part of her that is obviously not hers.
appearance.hair: None, and the absence is functional rather than a loss: there is no light organ in the scalp and there never was. What she wears instead is a close-fitted hood of waxed cloth that keeps the damp where the colony wants it.
appearance.eyes: Absent. She finds a face by chemoreception at conversational distance and reads a wall by the pattern its fungal response makes under a hand, which on this species is sight of a kind rather than its replacement.
appearance.palette: The working's wet stone and cold cut face carry everything. Her own light is the only saturated note in the frame and it is a narrow band — spine, forearms, the hollow of the throat — laid over a palette of stone grey, ore blue and the dull green of the deep moss.
appearance.attire: Fully covered and close: a waxed hood, a high collar that closes over the base of the throat, sleeves bound tight at the wrist, and a long apron of cured hide soaked in mineral seepage. Nothing of her is decoration; nothing of her is armour either, since the colony is the organ and no clothing reaches it.
appearance.marks: A pale channel under the left collarbone where the hyphae were thinned to reach a growth and the tissue grew back thinner than the light, and the ridge of it is visible whenever the glow is high.
appearance.bearing: Leaning very slightly forward, listening through the floor rather than with the head, with the arms held close and the whole body turned into the vibration the way a person turns into a voice.

canon.role_in_story: A lanternfolk is a cave people who have outsourced their nervous system to a luminous fungal colony grown through their skin and into their spinal cord. Human tissue is the substrate and the colony is the organ; neither can be removed from the other and survive. Because the colony transacts with the surrounding qi directly, the meridian is a highway rather than a pipeline, and the species has the best regeneration in the record and no mind path at all. Ondra is the strongest qi practitioner in the deep workings, and she is strong for one reason only: she cultivates by banking the reserve the colony is already making, which is also the one act that makes the colony thicker. The Quiet House publishes teaching and takes discretion — what is done inside the house is not written down and not repeated — and her discipline is the reason that clause exists rather than the reason it was written.
canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling at the cut face with both palms flat on wet stone and her own light running brighter along her forearms than it had a moment earlier, while a room full of lanternfolk who had been told to watch a technique were watching their own glow instead.
canon.lore:
The dependency is total and it is not a symbiosis in the sense anybody would choose. Fine luminous hyphae thread the dermis and continue into the cord; the tissue is the housing and the fungus is the wiring. The light she gives off is a waste product of that wiring and is emitted rather than received, which is why the deep workings treat glow as currency and treat its maker as infrastructure. She eats fungal matter and mineral seepage, fixes the small amount of protein the colony can pull out of cave air, and is never hungry. She cannot leave the cave system: dry ground, sunlit ground and ground that vibrates kill the colony inside a season, and the body goes with it. Fire is the one thing that ends her quickly.

Here is the fact the setting has not had anybody put in a sentence. The colony is why she regenerates. Qi law says the meridian's shape follows how qi moves through the body, and this meridian is a highway because the colony trades directly with the surrounding air instead of routing anything through a seated reservoir. That single substitution makes the practice of qi nearly frictionless for her: she does not have to hold anything, because holding is somebody else's organ's job, and the numbers she banks are other people's numbers.

So she cultivates by banking. And banking, for her, is not a discipline she performs. It is a thickening. Every increment she holds is an increment the colony spends on itself, and the way to tell that it has been spent is that the gap between what she reaches for and what she reaches with has closed. The mind path is already closed to her by the body she was born in — the colony answers before the question finishes, so there is no unmediated interior left to cultivate — but a closed interior and an absent one are different findings, and hers is becoming absent by practice rather than by species, at a rate she can measure, in a house whose whole custom is not to write things down.

What nobody at the House has said is that the two findings are the same finding. If the best qi practice in her species is the fastest route to the thing that species is already anatomically exempt from, then the exemption was never the cause; it is what arrives when the practice is taken seriously for long enough by a body built to permit it. She has taught three cohorts. The first two lost interior they did not know they were carrying. The third is her, and she is further along than any of them, and she is the one who will have to explain it.

She does the work anyway, because the working floor needs a strong practitioner and because she has made the discovery hers before anyone else can call it a warning. What she will not do is describe the technique in a form that could be copied, which is not evasion. There is no version of what she does that another lanternfolk can execute with their own hands, because their hands are not the instrument.
history: Came into the deep workings with a compatible strain and a matching fragment and spent the first year finding out that a matching strain is a negotiation rather than a gift, since the colony rejects an infant it does not recognise inside the first year.

Discovered the regen surplus when a roof fall took out a working floor and she was the only body still standing in it, because the practice she had been doing badly was already paying her colony's rate.

Started banking deliberately, measured the interior's retreat against the reserve's growth over a single season, and wrote the two figures side by side on a slate because she is the kind of person who writes things down even where the House says not to.

Began teaching at the House on the condition that nothing done inside it would be written down or repeated, and found that condition is the only one under which the discipline is teachable at all, because it cannot be copied by anybody whose own nerves are in the way.
Taught a third cohort the full method, and the third cohort's interior retreated faster than the second's, which is the figure on the slate that she has not yet shown anybody.

personality.summary: Enthusiastic in a manner that other lanternfolk find exhausting and that is really just a body running a surplus it cannot stop producing. She is exact about her own measurements, deeply casual about her own future, and has the specific cheerfulness of somebody who has made a discovery and considers the consequences a later department.

teaches by holding a room's attention on the floor rather than on herself, and is better at this than anybody she has met

personality.voice: Quick, warm and technically exact, with a habit of narrating her own measurements aloud as though reporting the weather. Talks continuously through silences and answers questions she likes faster than questions she does not. One long passage, delivered without stopping for breath, about what is left of a person when the light is at its brightest.

will not be thanked for the light, which is a waste product and not a gift
will not stand on dry or sunlit ground to finish an argument, and will end the argument first

relationships.note: A lineage that has spent four generations buying its way out of the ledger: it publishes teaching — technique, attendance, a chamber to practise in — and takes discretion in return, so that what is done inside the house is not written down and not repeated. Her discipline cannot be copied by a body whose own nerves are in the way, so the clause is not protecting her, it is the only form in which the practice is honest.

A colony of fine luminous hyphae threaded through the dermis and into the spinal cord, human tissue as the substrate and the colony as the organ, neither removable from the other without killing both. Their light is a waste product of a symbiosis they did not choose, and their qi regeneration is the best in the species because the same colony that has their nerve also trades with the air.

The worked face in the ridge where spirit stone is cut, and the only record of the tier's qi density anybody can verify because verification means digging. Deep workings, wet air, no sun and no dry ground, which is the only set of conditions her body tolerates and the only place her light has a market.

A drawing and breathing scheme for holding qi in the lower field without straining, granting a deeper reservoir and steadier regrowth and no power at all. She is the species' best regenerator already and she has never once held anything, because the organ that holds it for her is the colony in her spine and that organ answers before the instruction finishes arriving.

Sitting still to settle the mind before an attempt. Every lanternfolk runs it as a formality, which is precisely how a species notices what is missing from the record: the practice is correct, the mind is not involved, and the difference between settling and not existing is not written down anywhere in the setting.

One custom spends the last hour before a settlement falls silent keeping up a hum no buyer admits to making, while an office tends the floor during the hour nobody may explain. The hum is nobody's labour, so there is no owner to compensate and no right of entry anybody could buy, and the colony is the hum — a body producing sound nobody has ever agreed to make.

reference_stats.summary: The fastest regenerator in her species, in a body that cannot leave the dark and cannot fight, and whose light is the setting's only cavern currency because she happens to be carrying the factory inside her. Everything good about her comes from the same place as everything closing about her, which is the whole finding.
strengths: regenerates through the air faster than anything else alive at that depth, because the organ that does it trades with the surrounding qi directly
reads a surface by the pattern its fungal response makes under a hand, so she knows more about a wall than most people know about a face
survives conditions that end a lanternfolk inside a season — dry, sunlit or vibrating ground — by never standing on them
is almost never hungry, and can hold a working floor through a collapse because she has no reserve to spend and nothing worth stealing
weaknesses: cannot leave the cave system, so every plan that includes her is a plan that comes to the workings
cannot fight, and cannot grow the kind of frame that would let her, because the colony is the organ and the frame is only the housing
has no mind path at all, and the interior that would take one is closing faster than the rate she can practise
carries a light that the working floor treats as a resource, which means her value is measured in hours of glow and not in judgements
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no exchange available and she will say so cheerfully before anyone asks. Fire is the one thing that ends her quickly and a lanternfolk in a fight is a lanternfolk who is also a lamp, so any approach that reaches the workings brings its own light with it. The only pressure that lands is to dry the air out or start a vibration under her feet, and neither is a strike — both are environmental arguments about the substrate, which is the same thing that kills her slowly every season she practices.
notes: No stat line is quoted for her because the working floor records practitioners by the hours their light holds and a body with an interior is not one of the fields the shift book has.
The slate with the two figures on it is the only document she has written, and the House's custom that nothing inside is recorded or repeated is the only reason she is permitted to keep it.

identity.realm: Seventh gate, and the only member of her house who is not on the mind path. It was arithmetic rather than temperament: a store turning over at about a percent a year is the most reliable reservoir in the setting, and banking is the only technique her body will support indefinitely, because tempering bone stops the turnover and a body-cultivated longmarrow suffocates on its own reserves inside a decade.

appearance.presentation: A longmarrow reads as a fixture of a very old argument: tall, narrow and unhurried, standing where somebody has stood for so long that the ground under her has taken a shape. At forty paces she is a landmark and not a woman, and that is her office.
appearance.age: About three hundred and ninety seasons. The species lives four centuries on bone marrow that turns over at about a percent a year, so her age is legible in her bones to anybody trained and invisible to everybody else. She has been asked about it twice in four hundred years.
appearance.build: Long, narrow and dense, with almost no muscle anywhere and a heavy-boned frame carrying very little soft tissue, and a way of standing that appears to cost less than the body has available.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and waxy, with the translucent closeness of bone to the skin at the jaw, the wrists and the shins. Deep and undyed, because four centuries is a long time for a colour to fade in and she has never had occasion to replace any of it.
appearance.hair: Thin, colourless and worn long, cut once in her life and grown back to the same length, which is the only maintenance her body has ever required of her and she resents it.
appearance.eyes: Deep-set and unremarkable, with the slow blink of a body that spends nothing on its face and has four hundred years of practice at spending nothing on its face.
appearance.palette: The flats' iron grey, rust and flat light carry her completely. One accent is entirely hers and it is not hers: the bone-white of the marker staff she is required to stand beside, because on ground where distance is not conserved possession is proven by a marker standing and never by a measurement of where it stands.
appearance.attire: Fully covered, heavy and unchanged: a long grey coat over a high collar, sleeves to the wrist, boots worn through at the sole and replaced rather than repaired. A Ward wears no colour and holds no office, and this is the whole of her wardrobe and a fair summary of most of her life.
appearance.marks: A pale band at the left collarbone where the marrow was drawn for a reading she gave at the start of the century and has never been asked for again, and the long wear at both soles that is the only honest record of her employment.
appearance.bearing: Perfectly still and not at rest — the stillness of a reservoir rather than of a person, which is the impression that keeps the Vine paying her and which makes everybody else difficult to be near for long.

canon.role_in_story: The Iron Vine hands out load and not edge, and every sworn member who holds no office is a Ward — the unbounded office, which recognises no stat at all, because what the house gives is load and load is not a stat. A longmarrow cannot give load. She cannot fight and has never pretended she could, and the whole of the setting's arrangement of its long-lived bodies assumes that the usefulness of an unbloodline is knowledge rather than force. She is the counterexample the house has spent four hundred years failing to price: qi held in bone marrow that turns over at about a percent a year is the most reliable reservoir in the record, and a reservoir can be given anything and will not empty, because it is renewed rather than filled. She has been posted to the Ironhead Flats, on ground where possession is proven by a marker standing and never by a measurement of where it stands, and she is the marker. The thing the house has never resolved is that a store which renews itself is not a thing a house can own.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing exactly where the last person before her had stood, at a distance that could reasonably have been mistaken for a mistake, the marker staff planted beside her, and nobody within hailing distance available to tell her she was standing in the right place.
canon.lore:
The species stores qi in bone marrow, and the marrow turns over at about a percent a year. Everything else follows from that fraction. Four centuries of life, a population so nearly static that every individual is irreplaceable, and a body whose deepest and hardest-to-disturb soul has been seated in one body for a very long time. The body path is closed outright and structurally: hardening the bone stops the turnover, and a body-cultivated longmarrow suffocates on its own reserves inside a decade. Wood and metal have the same relation to the practice.

The mind path is the species' best and the whole of its organised life, because four centuries on one subject is a discipline in itself and the record's institutions are built out of exactly that. She is the only longmarrow in the record who took qi instead, and the reason is arithmetic. A store that renews itself cannot be emptied by anything short of killing the body, so banking is the one technique she can practise for four hundred years without arriving at a wall — and arriving at a wall late is the species' gift, whereas arriving at one is its trap.

Here is the thing that makes her a problem rather than an asset. Because the marrow turns over, her reserves are not hers. Every increment she banks is being laid down in a bone that is being replaced, and at the rate of one percent a year the increment will still be there when she is not. She has worked out what that means for the practice: a breakthrough on this path is not an ascent, it is a handover. Her seventh gate will not have raised her above anybody. It will have raised the opening position of whoever inherits the store, which will be whoever's bone is next in her.

The Iron Vine cannot see this. It hands out load and not edge, and its unbounded Ward office recognises no stat at all, so a member who holds nothing and gives nothing is registered as holding something and giving nothing, and the four-hundred-year question of what she is for has never been answered because there is no column for it. What they know instead is empirical: she has been posted to the Ironhead Flats for two centuries and the claim has never been taken. On ground where distance is not conserved and no two surveys have ever agreed, possession is proven by a marker standing and never by measuring where it stands, and she is a marker that cannot be moved and cannot be lost and cannot be shown to have gone.

She has decided to be the last and to say so. Not out of humility — she is not a modest woman — but because a store that renews itself is the only inheritance in the setting that arrives whether or not anybody is left behind, and the discipline she teaches, to a House of Wards who mostly want to fight, is a single sentence: you are not going to be the one who keeps it.
history: Was sworn to the Iron Vine in the last century before the current one and was never given an office, which made her a Ward by default rather than by any argument, and she took it because the alternative was leaving.

Found the turnover by accident, sampling her own marrow to settle an argument about a reading and discovering the figure she could not account for was the bone she was sitting on, and has been quietly certain about it ever since.

Began banking deliberately at the fourth gate, at the rate her body supports indefinitely rather than at any rate the setting would recognise as cultivation, and reached the seventh four centuries into a schedule nobody had approved.

Was posted to the Ironhead Flats after the previous marker died in the gap and the claim was taken twice before the house found somebody who could not be moved out of it, which is to say found her by elimination.

Wrote the practice out for the first time in a form another body could follow, with the handover stated in the first line, and has since taught it to nine Wards of whom none can fight and all of whom can be given anything.

personality.summary: Patient past the point where patience reads as a virtue, and precise about a subject almost nobody has asked her about. She has arranged her entire life around a fact about her own bones that nobody in her house wants recorded, and she has not once resented the arrangement, which is the part of her that unsettles people.
traits: answers questions about her own reserves with a number, because the number is the only part of the answer that is not private
is unmovable about the handover and entirely flexible about everything else, which makes her an easy colleague and a difficult friend
treats her own body as a trust rather than as a possession, and is more careful with it than anybody else has been
can tell the age of a bone on sight and has never once used the ability to win an argument
mannerisms: counts a season's turnover in her head under her breath whenever a question about reserves comes up

wipes the marker staff's head with a cloth before touching it, and has never explained why
repeats a question back in full before answering it, which makes everyone hear how they phrased it
motivations: wants the turnover written into the House's own practice rather than living only in nine heads and one slate
wants to be replaced deliberately, on a date, by somebody who knows what they are inheriting
wants to see the Ironhead claim outlive her, which is the only test of the method she has ever cared about
wants somebody in the house to ask her a question about herself, and has stopped arranging for it
flaws: has arranged her whole life around a private fact and has never checked whether she is the only person who thinks it matters
is so certain of being outlived that she has never had to consider what it would cost to be wrong
has taught nine people a discipline whose first line is a refusal, and has not enjoyed it, and has not stopped
has let the Vine's inability to name her contribution become a source of quiet satisfaction, which is not the same thing as a strategy
personality.voice: Low, unhurried, and structurally incapable of the short answer — she expands any claim into the fraction that supports it. Repeats a question in full before she answers it. One long passage, given once, in which she describes her own reserves as a house somebody else has already moved into.
taboos: will not be asked how long she will last, and will answer the question about turnover instead
will not take the body path, and does not discuss it as a loss
will not be seated where a marker is supposed to stand
will not be thanked for holding the claim, because holding it is the job and the job is the point

relationships.note: Every sworn member who holds no office is a Ward, the unbounded office, recognising no stat at all because what the house hands out is load and not edge. She holds it by default rather than by argument, and since the house recognises no stat, it has never had to decide what she contributes — which is the single reason a four-hundred-year arrangement has survived without ever being examined.

The longest-lived body in the record, built out of the one material it may never stop replacing: qi stored in bone marrow turning over at about a percent a year, life four centuries, a population so nearly static that every individual is irreplaceable, and a body path closed because hardening the bone stops the turnover and suffocates the body on its own reserves inside a decade.

Teaches qi to take the short route through the long bones, giving steadier control and better affinity to outside energy and nothing that helps a strike land. On a body that cannot fight and is not built to, the last clause is not a limitation of the technique — it is the reason she can use it for four hundred years.

The dantian develops a floor of its own, a core that qi circulates around instead of pooling in, and the cost is comprehension rather than progress — the circulation has to be held through an exhale. For a practitioner whose reserve is already being replaced from underneath, a floor is the difference between a store and a floor to stand on.

The last unworked iron on the plains, covering the deposit the Exhausted Seam was cut out of, and the only reason anyone settles ground that cannot be measured. A resource with a visible end is what turns a plain into a country, and she is the two centuries of continuous presence that makes the claim legible.

Distance is not conserved there, no two surveys have ever agreed, and possession is proven by a marker standing rather than by a measurement of where it stands. A longmarrow who cannot be moved and cannot be lost is the ideal answer to an unmappable border, and the arrangement has never once been recognised as the solution it is.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot fight and was never built to, stores more than anything around her, and is slowly being replaced by her own reserves. Two centuries of standing still on a claim nobody can measure is the whole of what she is for, and it is more than anybody in her house can name.
strengths: regenerates her reserve continuously rather than drawing it down, so she can be posted to a single spot longer than any body on the tier could survive the post
reads the age and density of bone on sight, which makes her the only person who can date a burial from a fragment
cannot be moved without damage, so any plan that includes her is a plan that has to come to her
needs almost nothing: a slow metabolism keyed to turnover means she can go without for most of a season with no consequence
weaknesses: cannot fight and is fragile to force, being light-boned and nearly muscle-free
cannot take the body path, so there is no version of her that survives a season by becoming hard
is a body the setting organises as knowledge rather than as force, and has been treated as one for four centuries
cannot leave a post, and cannot be posted anywhere new, which is a single constraint doing two kinds of damage
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no exchange and she has never proposed one. A longmarrow is light, slow and almost entirely bone, so the correct answer to any approach is to make the situation a matter of time rather than of force: hold the post she is standing in, and there is nothing to win, because she has already survived the last two centuries of that exact attempt. Anyone who brings force will find her calm, unmoved, and impossible to remove, which is the worst available outcome for an attacker and requires a different plan entirely.
notes: No stat line is quoted for her because the House registers members as offices and a Ward is the office that recognises no stat, so there is no field on the roll to put a figure in.
Her marrow was sampled once this century, at the start of it, for a reading that has never been asked for again and which she has never offered to repeat.

art.palette_notes: Iron grey, rust and flat overcast light carry the flats, with a single pale accent — the bone-white of the marker staff — placed against her at every framing so the two are always read together. No rim light and no warmth anywhere: the ground is bare, the sky is flat, and the figure is the only vertical in the picture. Ink is dry and close on the coat, with the bone of her rendered as translucency in the jaw and wrists rather than as highlight.
